A Mini-Blog in Neuromorphic Computing Security
items.summary: A short literature review of security in neuromorphic computing, focused on spiking neural networks (SNNs). It covers software-layer attacks (such as adversarial noise) and hardware-layer attacks (such as voltage and fault injection on neuron circuits), along with consolidated studies that propose defenses against the attacks. It also includes software and hardware threats that overlap, as attacks on neuromorphic algorithms are shaped by the constraints of the hardware that runs them. Written as a self-directed literature review, not original experimental research or extensive analysis.

items.summary: This third volume continues the series by addressing the computational realisation of Riemannian structures on latent manifolds and their integration with equivariant architectures and stochastic dynamics. It treats discrete differential geometry on graphs and meshes, numerical approximations of the Levi-Civita connection and curvature, Riemannian Langevin dynamics and stochastic gradient flows, and the systematic incorporation of geometric priors through equivariant neural networks and geometric deep learning. The discussion emphasises practical consequences for the design, training, and analysis of geometric world models, including JEPA-style predictors and spatial intelligence systems.

A helical hopping network built only from s orbitals can support an itinerant orbital moment and an orbital Edelstein response, but such a basis has no local atomic OAM and therefore omits the complementary contribution arising from coherence among active p orbitals. Here we construct a six-band multiorbital double helix model parameterized by characteristic B form DNA geometry…

items.title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
items.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) explain foundation model representations by decomposing activations into sparse combinations of learned dictionary atoms. However, the learned dictionaries can vary across training runs, limiting the reliability and reproducibility of SAE-based analyses. We propose Consistent Sparse Dictionary Learning (ConSDL), which replaces the standard linear encoder with per-sample sparse coding. This is motivated by our synthetic analysis showing that coefficients from a single linear encoder pass are suboptimal compared with those obtained by per-sample optimization, suggesting that sparse coding is a reliable mechanism for dictionary learning. items.title: A Topological Quantum Field Theory for Representation Varieties of Torus Links
items.summary: We construct a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) that computes the virtual classes of $G$-representation varieties associated with the fundamental group of a torus link complement. Following the framework established by González-Prieto, Logares and Muñoz for $G$-representation varieties of surface groups, we introduce a suitable bordism whose iteration enables a recursive topological evaluation of these virtual classes. Via this TQFT, we explicitly compute the virtual class of these varieties for the groups $G=\mathrm{AGL}_1(\mathbb{C})$ and $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$.

items.title: Diversity Without Labels: Task-Agnostic Coreset Selection Across Perception and Action
items.summary: While data collection for model training is relatively easy, curating high-quality datasets from large collections is inherently challenging. Coreset estimation methods address this problem by identifying the best data subsets to train models on. However, existing approaches often require proxy model training, extensive annotations, or task-specific tailoring. Unsupervised alternatives typically exploit geometric properties in foundation model feature spaces, but are limited to pairwise image-to-image comparisons or comparisons against a fixed subset. We introduce CoreDNA, an unsupervised, task-agnostic coreset estimation approach that pools neuron activations from vision foundation models…

items.title: Foundation-Model-Driven 3D Scene Graphs for Mobile Manipulation
items.summary: Geometric and Semantic Foundation models are becoming increasingly popular tools for generating spatial maps for robots. Recent work (e.g., FOUND-IT) has leveraged these tools to construct real-time, task-driven, and open-set 3D scene graphs from a single uncalibrated camera. However, while classical robot mapping techniques have undergone extensive system demonstrations, limited work has been done to develop both the fundamental and the systems wide advancements needed to integrate these new types of robot spatial memory into a full, useable autonomy pipeline. In this paper, we bridge this gap, and in doing so we also evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of this type of 3D memory.…

items.title: Timelike entanglement entropy with gravitational anomaly from complexified geometry
items.summary: We investigate the timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) in a two-dimensional conformal field theory with a gravitational anomaly, $c_L\neq c_R$, dual to topologically massive gravity in AdS$_3$. Holographically, the TEE is determined by the on-shell action of a massive spinning particle on a single complex geodesic anchored at the endpoints of the timelike interval. This action consists of the complex geodesic length and the twist of a parallel-transported normal frame. We carry out the computation in Poincaré AdS$_3$, non-extremal and extremal rotating BTZ backgrounds, and provide an equivalent Chern-Simons derivation in which the bulk connection stays real while only the saddle of the…

items.title: QD-Rec: Open-Ended Evolution of Recommendations via Quality-Diversity
items.summary: Open-ended search combined with foundation models has produced advances such as faster algorithms, new results on open mathematical problems, and self-improving agents. We extend this paradigm to recommendation for decision-making, focusing on decisions where the set of possible choices is fixed but the reasons for choosing them are not. In high-stakes decisions, e.g., which company to acquire or which customer to target, comparing diverse, well-reasoned options can be more useful than a single ranked list. We formalize open-ended recommendation as building a diverse, high-quality set of recommendations, each an item together with a hypothesis, a natural-language reason why the item fits…

items.title: AWM: An All-in-One Wireless Foundation Model for Multi-User Channel Acquisition and Localization Without Downstream Tuning
items.summary: Wireless foundation models (WFMs) seek to unify diverse wireless tasks and scenarios, yet existing methods still rely on task- or scenario-specific components or deployment-time fine-tuning. This paper presents an all-in-one wireless model (AWM), a WFM that unifies multi-user channel acquisition and localization, despite their distinct data modalities and functional objectives. We reveal that user location and channel state information (CSI) at different frequencies can be viewed as attribute-specific measurements of the same wireless link. By introducing in-scenario same-attribute reference pairs as prompts, AWM converts heterogeneous attributes into alignable relativity representations,…

items.title: Foundation-Model Supervision of Distilled Potentials for Million-Atom Molecular Dynamics
items.summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials distilled from foundation models enable fast large-scale molecular dynamics (MD), but they can fail locally in chemical environments that their training data did not sample. System-averaged error metrics and small random audits often miss such sparse or isolated failures. Here we use an exact equivariant foundation model, MACE-MPA-0, to check every atom of million-atom production simulations. Reorganizing two-layer MACE inference into a receiver-chunked three-pass schedule that keeps no per-edge intermediates resident reduces the marginal memory per atom 340-fold, evaluates up to $2.86\times10^{7}$ atoms on a single H200 GPU, and supervises…

items.title: Language Models Learn to Improve Language Models
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to automate AI research, including language-model (LM) development, offering a potential path toward recursive self-improvement. However, turning experimental feedback into a learned ability to propose effective improvements across models faces two challenges. First, training such an ability with real feedback is expensive: reinforcement learning (RL) requires evaluating tens of thousands of proposals, each potentially requiring a full model-training run. Even at ten GPU-hours per run, reward collection alone would consume hundreds of thousands of GPU-hours, motivating a cheaper surrogate. Second, surrogate feedback can become unreliable…

items.title: On the center of the Clifford Algebra
items.summary: The center of a Clifford algebra associated to a non-degenerate quadratic form over a field is described in the existing literature, but an elementary proof of the result seems lacking. The aim of this paper is to provide such an elementary proof.

items.title: MLLM Frame Subset Ensembling for Audio-Visual Video QA and MLLM-based Reranking for Ad-hoc Video Search in TRECVID 2025
items.summary: This paper presents the overview of the runs related to the Ad-hoc Video Search (AVS) and Video Question Answering (VQA) tracks of TRECVID 2025 on behalf of the CERTH-ITI team. For the AVS track, we introduce a two-stage framework built on foundation models. In the first stage, multiple vision-language models (VLMs) encode both the input query, augmented through LLM-generated rephrasings, and the candidate video shots, producing weighted similarity scores for initial retrieval. In the second stage, we utilize a Multimodal-LLM(MLLM)-based reranking module that evaluates the semantic alignment between each shot among the top-N highest-ranked ones and the original query, generating updated…

items.title: Nonergodicity from Hilbert-Subspace Cloning
items.summary: We identify a class of nonintegrable quantum many-body systems composed of single Pauli strings that possess an extensive number of noncommuting local conserved quantities and exhibit partial ergodicity breaking due to exponentially degenerate energy spectra. We show that such systems exhibit a novel mechanism, Hilbert-subspace cloning, where the identical chaotic Hamiltonian acts on each of exponentially many disconnected Hilbert subspaces. Although the dynamics within each clone thermalizes, quantum coherence between clones remains protected and detectable by local observables. Consequently, the long-time behavior of local observables is described by a coherence-preserving partial Gibbs…

items.title: LWMa: Distributed Deployment of an Angle-Delay-Domain Wireless Foundation Model for Multiple Tasks
items.summary: The growing diversity of wireless services in sixth-generation (6G) wireless communication systems calls for reusable channel representations that support multiple tasks across different propagation environments. However, deploying such representations between user equipment and the base station in frequency-division duplexing systems faces uplink feedback constraints. This paper proposes a distributed framework based on an angle-delay-domain large wireless model (LWMa) for multiple tasks. LWMa exploits angle-delay structure and delay truncation to improve feature extraction and reduce computational cost. A scenario-specific network inspired by Perceiver IO (input-output) compresses…

items.title: Path to Prior-Data Fitted Relational Models via Learned Latent Multi-table Representations
items.summary: Prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) show that pretraining on large populations of synthetic tasks can enable generalization to unseen datasets with little or no downstream fine-tuning. This paradigm is effective for transformer-based tabular and relational foundation models such as RDB-PFN, but remains largely unexplored for graph-based relational models built on message passing. We pretrain the graph-based relational foundation model Griffin on large collections of synthetic relational databases and ask whether curriculum learning, which benefits transformer-based relational learners, also improves message-passing representations. Rather than fine-tune on downstream tasks, we use the…

items.title: Foundation Models for Autonomous Space Robotics: Architectures, Physical Adaptation, and Validation
items.summary: Space robots must interpret tasks and act despite unfamiliar dynamics, difficult sensing conditions, and limited opportunities for human intervention. Foundation models offer reusable perceptual and behavioral knowledge, but their value depends on how that knowledge reaches physical execution. This critical review follows space-specific requirements through perception, prediction, planning, and action to deployment and validation, emphasizing orbital manipulation and proximity operations. Terrestrial comparisons establish benefits of particular pretraining stages and model interfaces; their transfer to space dynamics and constrained onboard operation remains insufficiently tested. Event…

items.title: Unifying Embodied Foundation Models via a Model-to-Policy Formulation
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models and world-action models (WAMs) have emerged as promising approaches to robot learning and control. These models integrate multimodal perception and action generation, but differ in their architectures, output representations, and learning objectives. In this paper, we present a unified, architecture-agnostic probabilistic formulation for embodied foundation models based on stochastic kernels. Our formulation has two key components: (i) we characterize embodied foundation models through conditional output distributions and action-realization kernels, which together induce task-conditioned robot policies; and (ii) we connect pretraining and post-training…

items.title: SpikeQ: Spike-Guided Post-Training Quantization for Spiking Neural Networks
items.summary: On neuromorphic chips, spiking neural networks (SNNs) consume far less energy than artificial neural networks (ANNs), but the limited memory of these chips requires low-bit synaptic weights and membrane potentials. Existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods provide them without retraining and, like those for ANNs, minimize numerical errors such as the mean squared error (MSE). In an SNN, however, a quantization error reaches later layers only through the spikes it flips. We find that errors of equal MSE can cause very different accuracy losses, whereas errors that flip the same fraction of spikes cause the same loss. We therefore propose SpikeQ, a spike-guided PTQ framework. For…

items.title: Adaptation of Computer Use Agents to New Software with User Manuals
items.summary: Recent advances in multimodal foundation models have significantly improved the ability to operate real-world software through graphical user interfaces (GUIs) using visual observations and natural language instructions. However, maintaining strong performance on unseen applications remains challenging, as practical tasks often require long-horizon procedural knowledge and application-specific operation patterns. In addition, constructing executable tasks and collecting corresponding trajectories for training still heavily rely on human-annotated data, incurring substantial cost. In this paper, we propose MAGE (Manual-augmented computer use AGent Execution and learning), a framework that…

items.title: A100: A Hybrid Vision Foundation Model for Agricultural Plant Image Analysis
items.summary: The use of accurate vision models for crop monitoring, disease diagnosis, and plant phenotyping in agriculture is hindered by the lack of expertly annotated data, especially in developing countries. We propose A100, an agricultural vision foundation model that is pre-trained using self-supervised learning on 3 million unlabeled images from fields covering more than 100 crop species. A100 uses a hybrid CNN-Transformer backbone that fuses MBConv stages for local feature extraction with Transformer stages for global contextual representation. A100 uses pre-training with the integration of DINO self-distillation, iBOT masked patch reconstruction, and KoLeo uniformity regularization, resulting…

items.summary: In their work on multiscalar RG flows, Rychkov and Stergiou posed the question of whether there exist real fixed points of the one-loop renormalization group for scalar field theories in $d=4-ε$ which respect no extra symmetry beyond the universal $\mathbb{Z}_2$ field inversion. In this note, we report on a construction of a large number of such fixed points in the theory of $22001$ scalar fields, thus resolving the question. The construction uses the geometry of an equiangular tight frame in order to reduce the (up to two-loop) fixed point equation to a two-dimensional space of couplings without assuming any extra symmetry. items.title: Unit-level aggregation breaks coverage in causal foundation models
items.summary: Causal foundation models (CFMs) show promising results for treatment-effect estimation, with unit-level estimates that are competitive on standard benchmarks. Many causal analyses, however, inform decisions through effects averaged over groups of units, such as the full sample, the treated units, or a subgroup, and for such decisions a CFM is useful only if its credible intervals are calibrated. We examine these intervals and find that their coverage degrades, both in simple synthetic settings and on standard benchmarks. items.summary: The proposition that living organisms operate not merely as diffusive biochemical engines, but as integrated, light-emitting, liquid-crystalline networks, represents one of the most provocative intersections in contemporary biophysics and quantum biology. Over the past half-century, experimental advancements involving cryogenic charge-coupled devices (CCDs), electron-multiplying CCDs (EMCCDs), and single-photon-counting photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) have established beyond dispute that all metabolically active biological tissues continuously radiate ultra-weak photon emissions (UPE), historically termed biophotons. items.title: Neuromorphic Event-Camera Imaging and Image Reconstruction
items.summary: Event cameras, also known as dynamic vision sensors, depart from the synchronous frame-based imaging paradigm by reporting per-pixel brightness changes asynchronously as a stream of events. Each event encodes a pixel coordinate, a microsecond-resolution timestamp, and the polarity of a logarithmic-intensity change that has crossed a contrast threshold. This principle yields microsecond temporal resolution, a dynamic range exceeding $120$~dB, sparse output, and very low power, making event cameras attractive for high-speed and high-dynamic-range scenarios in which conventional cameras suffer from motion blur and saturation. items.title: Network Geometry of Neural Processing Components for Interpretable AI in Sparse Neuromorphic Dendritic Circuits
items.summary: Neuromorphic AI increasingly draws on sparse dendritic computation, yet a network-science framework linking sub-neuronal circuit organization to function remains underdeveloped. Here we introduce the neural processing component (NPC) paradigm, representing synapses, dendrites, somata and axons as network elements whose sparse topology shapes computation. We implement this paradigm in a dendritic reservoir-based network for trajectory detection, demonstrating in device-informed simulations that real-time motion trajectories can be detected through fixed NPC design rather than training. items.title: Input- and Feature-Space Correction for Cross-Hospital IHC Grading
items.summary: Pathology foundation models (FMs) are trained predominantly on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images but are increasingly used as frozen feature extractors for immunohistochemistry (IHC), where cross-hospital differences can impair grading. However, systematic comparisons of correction methods for cross-hospital IHC grading remain limited. To address this gap, we benchmark label-free transformations applied to input images before frozen-FM encoding and to features after frozen-FM encoding using UNI and Virchow2, three IHC markers, and six directed cross-hospital transfers, yielding 12 settings. items.title: Civilizational Unbinding Transition and the Demise of Human Warfare in the Superintelligence (SI) Society
items.summary: Abstract For millennia, large-scale inter-group violent conflict has been treated as an ineradicable structural feature of human civilization, with war mortality assumed to only follow a gradual, asymptotic downward trajectory. This study introduces the ‌Civilizational Unbinding Index (U)‌, a quantifiable framework that measures the progressive relaxation of natural, social and survival constraints across 10,000 years of human history, validated against the fully open Seshat Global History Databank. The present paper focuses on the mathematical structure of that bound state. items.summary: Abstract Predicting the long-horizon collective dissolution, continuous escape trajectories, and evaporation timescales of massive gravitational swarms in relativistic environments is a foundational challenge in celestial mechanics and computational astrodynamics. Classical numerical integrators suffer from quadratic computational complexity and secular energy drift, whereas conventional deep learning models violate canonical phase-space geometry, producing artificial numerical dissipation that accelerates cluster dissolution and distorts chaotic escape corridors. items.title: A Logging-Constrained Spatial Registration Framework for Transparent Geological Modeling of Underground Coal Mines
items.summary: Abstract Spatial inconsistency between borehole trajectory, logging measurements and geological horizons is a critical bottleneck in transparent geological modeling of underground coal mines, yet these components are conventionally treated as independent workflows. Here we present a logging-constrained spatial registration framework that integrates full-attitude quaternion updating with weak geological self-correction in a unified optimization model. While narrowband photodetectors effectively suppress optical background interference, their spectral selectivity is generally predetermined by material composition or device geometry, preventing adaptive spectral perception within a single hardware platform. Advancing chemical reaction prediction in data-scarce drug discovery with active and geometric deep learning.
items.summary: The success of generative molecular design depends on the synthetic accessibility of the molecules it creates. While computational models can help predict chemical reactions, their current effectiveness is limited by a lack of reference data and the difficulty of accurately predicting reaction regioselectivity. Here, to address this, we present an integrated closed-loop workflow that combines efficient reaction data acquisition with high-accuracy deep learning. items.title: Where the Loop Meets the Budget: Analyzing On-Device Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Language-model systems now rewrite their own memory, code, and weights, and small language models now run on phones and embedded boards. This paper asks whether the two developments have met: can a system improve itself within the memory, energy, thermal, latency, and connectivity budgets of a device? We define edge self-improvement as a verified update loop under a timevarying device budget, and we classify 63 works along three axes: the improved component, where computation ran in the reported evaluation, and the verification tier. Beyond Linear Causality: The Cosmological Uroboros Framework (CUF) as a Conceptual Ontological Schema

Built upon three fundamental nodes—Artificial Superintelligence (ASI, A), the physical Universe (U), and a technologically capable Cognitive Agent (C)—the model establishes a closed ontological fixpoint described by the conceptual, systems-theoretic recursive relation A* = f(g(h(A*))), where each entity serves as the formal qualitative boundary condition for the next. items.title: Quantum Biology 2.0: Traversing and harnessing protein superhighway networks of light and life.
items.summary: As an emergent field stimulated by insights from the biological, chemical, physical, and quantum sciences, quantum biology explores how quantum phenomena such as superradiance, tunneling, and entanglement can be leveraged to enhance, influence, and probe biological processes across a diversity of scales and physical degrees of freedom. This review surveys key theoretical, computational, and experimental developments over the last decade, providing relevant historical background and scientific context going back as far as Bohr's 1932 lecture on "Light and Life" in Copenhagen. Reflecting major new areas of investigation, biophysical intuitions, and advancements in critical areas of study…

items.title: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: A Survey
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) seeks to turn gains in an AI system into a stronger capacity to produce subsequent gains. Foundation models make parts of this process practical through generated training data, program revision and automated experimentation, but repeated optimization alone does not establish recursive improvement. This survey organizes the field around two overlapping goals: automated design of AI infrastructure, and repair and optimization of existing systems. We relate these goals to AutoML, meta-learning and program search, and formulate their objectives alongside criteria for task gains, retained capabilities and improved update procedures. items.summary: Hyperbolic geometry explains many structural features of real-world networks, yet existing hyperbolic generative network models with community organization such as the nonuniform popularity-similarity optimization (nPSO) are restricted to unipartite graphs. Here we introduce a bipartite extension of the nPSO model called nBPSO, motivated by the prevalence of community organization in real-world bipartite networks and the emerging evidence of hyperbolic hierarchical connectivity in trained sparse neural networks. nBPSO provides explicit control over link density, degree distribution, average clustering, and community organization. items.title: Experimental platform to study the neuronal mechanisms of magnetoreception in the honey bee.
items.summary: Honey bees (Apis mellifera) offer an alternative model for investigating magnetoreception, exhibiting reliable navigation and behavioral responses to magnetic fields. Thanks to their compact brains, well-matched to the penetration depth of modern optical imaging techniques, they may offer insights into the neural and biochemical mechanisms underlying this sense, something that standard models, like migrating birds, have not so far provided. But also in honeybees, this progress requires tools capable of resolving weak, magnetically induced neural activity with high spatio-temporal precision. items.summary: Superintelligence is usually defined as a machine intellect that exceeds human cognition across most domains. That framing conflates three distinct properties: computational capability, warranted knowledge, and legitimate authority. This article develops a systems definition suited to large language models, tool-using agents, databases, theorem provers, and other computational knowledge artifacts. Using conceptual synthesis and constructive requirement derivation, we distinguish a computational artifact, an operational self that preserves commitments and consequence history, and a normative principal that holds purpose and accountability. items.title: Neural state reduction: a quantum-inspired framework for how latent conscious thought becomes reportable.

items.title: Quantum coherent dynamics in allophycocyanin trimer complex.
items.summary: For years, scientists have debated whether plants and algae use quantum coherence to enhance the transfer of light energy during photosynthesis. Some studies have suggested that wavelike quantum effects might help energy flow more efficiently between pigments. To investigate this idea, we studied allophycocyanin (APC), a light-harvesting protein complex found in cyanobacteria. Using a combination of ultrafast laser spectroscopic methods and rigorous hierarchical equations-of-motion simulations, we examined both the trimer protein complex and its monomer subunit.
